title: Derive feature names from produce/consume artifacts as {verb}-{domain|resource}

facts.note: Task text mentions naming features or produce/consume artifacts; illustrative signal, not a scope gate.
Typical places where feature names sit next to produce/consume artifacts; illustrative signals only.
Needs a diff-level observer that sees new or renamed feature names alongside the artifacts they work with.
Artifact type, domain/resource decomposition, focus and verb fit require semantic judgement.

fires: A feature is being named for an artifact it produces or consumes (event, state, data or config) in a plan, manifest, doc or acceptance.
A feature is renamed or its name is reviewed against the artifacts it produces/consumes.
A new produce/consume artifact is introduced and the feature that works with it must be seeded.
doesNotFire: Naming the artifact itself (its domain:resource name) — governed by the naming-patterns convention.
Coder-side naming of functions, files or variables inside an implementation.
Editing a feature's acceptances or description without touching its name or artifacts.

given: A feature produces/consumes artifacts (WHAT: entities, states, events); features are HOW (actions, capabilities).
when: You derive, add, rename or review the feature's name.
then: Name it {verb}-{domain} if it acts on the entire domain, {verb}-{resource} if on a specific resource within the domain; choose the verb by artifact type (event, state, data, config).
prefer: Typical verbs (not closed lists): events (past tense: ended, started, closed) → publish, emit, start, close, trigger; states (adjectives: remaining, active, current) → track, monitor, maintain, update; data (nouns: choice, identity, profile) → create, manage, process, handle, make; configs (config, settings, agreement) → configure, setup, initialize, define.
Another verb that fits better is fine, e.g. the verb form of the artifact (identity → identify-<domain>).
Identify domain and resource from the artifact's meaning; in a nested name the domain is not necessarily the part before the colon.
avoid: Naming the feature after the artifact (WHAT) instead of an action (HOW) on it.
A verb that does not fit the artifact's type and meaning.
Resource as object when the feature acts on the whole domain, or domain when it targets one resource.
why: A consistent WHAT→HOW transformation makes feature names derivable from artifacts so the plan stays coherent.
evidence: Each feature name is {verb}-{noun}, where the noun is the domain or the resource of one of its produce/consume artifacts.
The verb fits the artifact type (event/state/data/config) and meaning — a typical verb from that family or another appropriate verb.

The domain-vs-resource choice matches the feature's focus (whole domain vs specific resource), with domain/resource identified as the artifact's meaning indicates (not assumed to be the colon prefix).
verifier_detail: Object rules: domain_as_object_pattern '{verb}-{domain}' — when: domain is the primary focus of the feature; rationale: feature acts on the entire domain. resource_as_object_pattern '{verb}-{resource}' — when: resource is the primary focus of the feature; rationale: feature acts on specific resource within domain.

Verb lists are typical_verbs, not exhaustive (source says 'verbs like'); do not flag a verb solely for being outside the list — e.g. player:identity -> identify-player uses a verb outside the data list. Domain/resource come from the source examples' parentheticals; the domain is not necessarily the part before the colon (mechanic:timebank.remaining has domain timebank; mechanic:decision.choice has domain decision). These are examples, not a general parsing rule for nested names.

Events (past tense: ended, started, closed) typical_verbs: publish, emit, start, close, trigger. Source examples: match:started (domain match, resource started) -> start-match; session:closed (domain session, resource closed) -> close-session.

States (adjectives: remaining, active, current) typical_verbs: track, monitor, maintain, update. Source examples: mechanic:timebank.remaining (domain timebank, resource remaining) -> track-timebank; session:active (domain session, resource active) -> maintain-session.

Data (nouns: choice, identity, profile) typical_verbs: create, manage, process, handle, make. Source examples: mechanic:decision.choice (domain decision, resource choice) -> make-choice (verb make + resource choice); player:identity (domain player, resource identity) -> identify-player.

Configs (config, settings, agreement) typical_verbs: configure, setup, initialize, define. Source examples: match:config (domain match, resource config) -> configure-match; league:config (domain league, resource config) -> define-league.
Verb selection depends on the event/state/data/config classification defined by planner.interface.naming-patterns (graph: requires).
